data.reason: WAN path is dead at gw.lan's own vtnet0: repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link down/up cycles in dmesg, 48211 output errors and 48211 packets dropped "no bufs" on vtnet0, ping/dhcp to the ISP gateway failing with ENOBUFS ("sendto error: 55", dhclient "send_packet: No buffer space available"), and an incomplete ARP entry for 198.51.100.1 while LAN (10.20.0.9) is fine. The modem side is healthy (cm_status OPERATIONAL, registration complete, min SNR 37.7 dB), so this is a stuck transmit queue on the firewall NIC, not a provider fault. A wan_reload cannot clear it — four reloads during this outage returned rc=0 without restoring traffic and the 24h reload cap (12/12) is already reached, so only a firewall reboot will re-initialize the interface. Maintainer is away tonight; requesting approval to proceed.

data.component: WAN NIC (vtnet0) transmit queue on the firewall
data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 got wedged (driver watchdog timeouts with link down/up cycles around 02:01), so its transmit queue stopped accepting packets — everything toward the ISP fails with ENOBUFS even though the modem itself is OPERATIONAL, and repeated DHCP reloads could not clear the stuck driver.
evidence: dmesg shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' interleaved with 'link state changed to DOWN/UP', indicating a stuck transmit queue on the WAN NIC
netstat -i: vtnet0 has 48211 Oerrs; netstat -s: '48211 output packets dropped due to no bufs, etc.' — the NIC stops accepting outbound frames

ping 198.51.100.1 and ping 8.8.8.8 from gw.lan both fail with 'sendto: No buffer space available' (ENOBUFS), while ping 10.20.0.9 on the LAN works normally — fault is at/beyond the WAN NIC, not the LAN
arp -a shows the ISP gateway 198.51.100.1 as '(incomplete)' — no ARP reply because frames never leave the wedged interface

/var/log/system/latest.log: dpinger 'WAN_DHCP 198.51.100.1: sendto error: 55' at 02:01:58 (matches outage start ~02:01), and dhclient repeatedly logs 'send_packet: No buffer space available' after each reload

/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json and events.jsonl: 4 reloads during this outage all returned rc=0 without restoring connectivity, and the 03:30 decision was action=none reason=reload_cap (12/12 max reloads in 24h)

modem-events.jsonl / modem-metrics.jsonl: modem logged 'registration complete' and reports cm_status OPERATIONAL with healthy SNR (~37.7 dB) — the provider link itself is fine, so a modem reboot or provider contact is not indicated
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall (firewall_reboot) to re-initialize the wedged vtnet0 driver; this was requested and ran (maintainer unreachable). A WAN reload alone cannot clear a stuck NIC queue, and the modem/provider side is healthy, so no provider action is needed. After boot, verify the default route responds (ping 198.51.100.1) and that ARP for the gateway resolves; if watchdog timeouts recur on this NIC, consider replacing/updating the virtio NIC or its driver.
